regime.summary: investors cut risk and bought government bonds
regime.headline: Risk-off / flight to quality
regime.paragraph: Investors cut risk and bought government bonds: US Treasury yields 2Y -5bp to 4.56% and 10Y -4bp to 4.94%. The US curve saw a bull steepener in 2s10s (+1bp to 38bp). The dollar was flat, gold fell 2.3%, the S&P 500 fell 1.8% and Brent fell 1.9%. US high-yield spreads widened 12bp. The standout move was USD/CNY (-0.2%, 2.9x its 20-day volatility).

regions.name: United States
regions.text: Treasuries rallied, 2Y -5bp to 4.56% and 10Y -4bp to 4.94%: a bull steepener (2s10s +1bp). Markets removed 8bp of Fed tightening over 12 months (now +56bp). The dollar was flat and the S&P 500 fell 1.8%.

regions.name: United Kingdom
regions.text: Gilts rallied with the front end leading, 2Y -6bp to 4.70% and 10Y -5bp to 5.28%: a bull steepener (2s10s +2bp). Markets removed 5bp of BoE tightening over 12 months (now +114bp). Sterling rose 0.2% and the FTSE 100 rose 0.1%.

regions.name: Europe
regions.text: Bunds rallied, 2Y -2bp to 3.06% and 10Y -2bp to 3.40%. BTP-Bund widened 7bp to 111bp. Markets removed 5bp of ECB tightening over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy (now +59bp). The euro was flat and the Euro Stoxx 50 fell 1.2%.

regions.name: Japan
regions.text: JGB 10Y yields fell 6bp to 2.817%, with 30Y -5bp. The yen strengthened as USD/JPY moved -0.1% to 157.70. Markets removed 2bp of BoJ tightening over 12 months on the bill-curve proxy (now +87bp). The Nikkei fell 0.1%.

regions.name: China
regions.text: CGB 10Y yields rose 1bp to 1.63%. The renminbi firmed with USD/CNY -0.21% at 6.6470. The CSI 300 fell 1.4% and copper fell 0.6%.

relationships.statement: Gold fell despite lower real yields.
relationships.lesson: Gold pays no coupon, so higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding it. A break often reflects central-bank buying, geopolitical hedging or dollar moves.

relationships.statement: Credit confirmed the equity sell-off as high-yield spreads widened.
relationships.lesson: Equities and credit both price corporate risk. When they disagree, credit (the more senior claim) is often the better signal.

relationships.statement: Wider BTP–Bund spreads indicated a higher Italian sovereign risk premium.
relationships.lesson: BTP–Bund is the euro area's main gauge of sovereign and fragmentation risk; it usually widens with risk-off and narrows when risk appetite is strong.

relationships.statement: Lower oil pulled US breakevens down.
relationships.lesson: Energy feeds directly into headline inflation, so short-dated breakevens track oil closely.

interview.question: Why did BTP–Bund spreads widen?
interview.answer: BTP–Bund moved +7bp to 111bp. The spread prices Italian sovereign credit and redenomination risk relative to Germany. It widens with global risk-off, Italian fiscal or political news, or a hawkish ECB (higher rates raise debt-servicing concerns), and tightens with strong risk appetite and carry demand. The ECB's TPI backstop limits disorderly widening. Today's Euro Stoxx move was -1.2%.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Federal Reserve, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 4.00%. Markets price a 70% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 2.2 hikes (56bp) over 12 months; terminal 4.71%. The 12-month pricing moved -8bp on the day. Method: Fed funds futures (CME FedWatch method). Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +56bp is 2.2 moves.

interview.question: How would you characterise today's market regime, and what's your evidence?
interview.answer: Risk-off / flight to quality: investors cut risk and bought government bonds. The classifier scores each regime's expected cross-asset signature against today's volatility-adjusted moves; the strongest factors were vol, equities, long end. Confidence: high. In an interview, lead with the conclusion, then two or three confirming moves, then the one asset that does not fit.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the European Central Bank, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 2.50%. Markets price a 86% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 2.4 hikes (59bp) over 12 months; terminal 3.23%. The 12-month pricing moved -5bp on the day. Method: Government bill-curve proxy (indicative). Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +59bp is 2.4 moves.

interview.question: What is driving JGB yields, and why does it matter globally?
interview.answer: JGB 10Y moved -6bp to 2.817% (a 1.9-sigma move). JGB yields reflect BoJ normalisation expectations and the pace of bond-buying reduction. Higher JGB yields can draw Japanese savings home, removing a marginal buyer of Treasuries and Bunds, which is why JGB moves can lift global term premia. USD/JPY moved -0.1%.
